(1) the directional bias of both lead and follower neural crest cells is necessary to maintain chain migration, (2) lead cells maintain contact with follower cells, but not vice versa, and (3) providing a path of lowest ECM resistance alone is insufficient to drive chain persistence.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the persistence of the chain migration phenomenon is a result of the interplay between the cell's ability to sense directional cues and to maintain cell-cell interactions, and that the persistence of this phenomenon is independent of the ECM.
the persistence of chain migration depends on the interplays of directional cell movement, biased cell contact and biased cell–ECM contact.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cell migration pattern is not only determined by the extracellular matrix, but also by the cell itself.
cell migration can be influenced by both the physical environment as well as cell-cell communication.
the cell chain migrates because the cells within the chain are biased to move towards the same target.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cell–cell contact does not drive chain migration persistence, but instead acts as a secondary mechanism that promotes chain migration.
the maintenance of cell chain migration is not simply a result of cell–cell contact but also requires directional bias towards the target.
cell–cell contacts and ECM cues are both important, but not sufficient to sustain chain migration.
